summary.oneLiner: Sinclairs Hotels Limited is a home-grown Indian hospitality brand operating hotels and resorts across ten leisure destinations in the country.
summary.business: Sinclairs Hotels Limited owns and operates hotels and resorts in India, serving domestic leisure travellers, destination weddings, conferences and corporate/MICE guests. The Company describes itself as a trusted and home-grown hospitality brand known for quality service, strong food offerings, hygienic operations and transparent business practices. As on March 31, 2026 it had a presence across ten destinations within the country and was in the process of further expansion, including through properties taken on lease.

currentContext.expansion: As on March 31, 2026 Sinclairs Hotels had a presence across ten destinations within the country and stated it is in the process of further expansion. During FY2025-26 the Company took on lease a palace-style resort with 90 rooms and fine villas, 'Sinclairs Palace Retreat Udaipur', and commenced operations there on 1st August, 2025 — consistent with the industry's gradual shift towards asset-light and lease-based operating models described in the MD&A. The Directors' Report states that the Company's cash reserves are very strong and that it is presently looking at opportunities to expand by way of both greenfield projects as well as acquiring existing properties on lease, with management continuing to evaluate capital-efficient growth opportunities to support long-term scalability while maintaining a prudent financial structure. Existing hotels and resorts at Siliguri, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Chalsa (Dooars) and Burdwan are described as well positioned to benefit from the West Bengal government's infrastructure roadmap for North Bengal and the hill regions, including a proposed Kolkata–Siliguri expressway. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in the routed text.

risks.note: The hospitality business is exposed to macroeconomic fluctuations, inflationary pressures and changes in discretionary consumer spending; any slowdown in economic growth could affect demand across leisure and business segments.

risks.risk: Weather and seasonality at key tourist destinations
risks.note: Adverse weather conditions at key tourist destinations can impact seasonality and occupancy levels — structurally relevant given the Company's leisure-destination footprint.
Rising costs relating to power, fuel, food inputs and employee expenses may impact operating margins.

risks.risk: Tax structure — high taxation and denial of input GST on room revenues
risks.note: High taxation levels and denial of input GST in hotel's room revenues pose a structural drag on hotel economics that the Company cannot control.
Regulatory changes and competitive intensity in certain markets are flagged as challenges to the business.

risks.risk: Geo-political developments and disruption in travel sentiment
risks.note: Geo-political developments or any disruption in travel sentiment could affect demand across leisure and business segments.

risks.risk: No formal risk management policy at company level
risks.note: The Directors' Report states that the policy on risk management is not applicable to the Company; mitigation relies on a proactive management approach — dynamic pricing, cost controls, manpower deployment, multi-skilling and monitoring of operating metrics — rather than a formal framework.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sinclairs Hotels Limited is a home-grown Indian hospitality brand operating hotels and resorts across ten leisure destinations in the country.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sinclairs Hotels Limited owns and operates hotels and resorts in India, serving domestic leisure travellers, destination weddings, conferences and corporate/MICE guests. The Company describes itself as a trusted and home-grown hospitality brand known for quality service, strong food offerings, hygienic operations and transparent business practices. As on March 31, 2026 it had a presence across ten destinations within the country and was in the process of further expansion, including through properties taken on lease.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Hotels and resorts:** Sinclairs Hotels & Resorts, Sinclairs Palace Retreat Udaipur

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic leisure travel and domestic tourism
- Destination weddings
- Conferences, corporate events and MICE
- North Bengal and the hill regions (Siliguri, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Chalsa/Dooars)
- West Bengal (including Burdwan)
- Rajasthan (Udaipur)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained domestic travel demand remained the primary growth driver, supported by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and a growing preference for experiential travel
- Continued momentum in MICE, destination weddings, conferences and corporate events supporting occupancy and revenue growth
- Recovery in international tourist arrivals expected to support revenue growth
- Improved air connectivity, expansion of regional airports and increased tourism promotion likely to augment demand across key destinations
- West Bengal government roadmap for large-scale infrastructure in North Bengal and the hill regions, and a proposed Kolkata–Siliguri expressway, seen as a catalyst for tourism at the Company's Siliguri, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Chalsa (Dooars) and Burdwan properties
- Industry shift towards asset-light and lease-based operating models, with operators optimising capital deployment and pursuing brand-led expansion in leisure and emerging destinations
- Margin headwind from rising power, fuel, food input and employee costs; high taxation and denial of input GST on hotel room revenues
- Management remains cautiously optimistic on growth prospects; hotels with strong brands, diverse geographic presence, high service standards and efficient cost structures are positioned to benefit

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Consolidate operations, improve operating efficiencies and strengthen presence across key destinations
- Pursue selective expansion — both greenfield projects and acquiring existing properties on lease — funded from strong cash reserves
- Evaluate capital-efficient growth opportunities to support long-term scalability while maintaining a prudent financial structure (no borrowings)
- Protect margins through dynamic pricing, tight cost controls, efficient manpower deployment and minimisation of wastage
- Multi-skill employees at unit level and adopt technology-driven processes with continuous monitoring of operating metrics across properties
- Run a target-based incentive policy for employees to spur sales growth and operational efficiency
- Focus on strengthening operational performance and enhancing guest experience
- Sustainability focus — optimise energy and water consumption, manage waste responsibly and reduce the environmental footprint of operations
- The Company is debt-free in its governance disclosures on payouts and distributes from profits: the Board recommended and the AGM notice proposes an ordinary resolution declaring a dividend of ₹0.80 per equity share of ₹2 each, i.e. 40% on the paid-up equity share capital, for the year ended March 31, 2026, to be paid out of the profits of the Company. Non-Executive Directors are remunerated only by sitting fees (₹5,000 per Board Meeting and ₹2,500 per Audit Committee Meeting), with the criteria for payments to non-executive directors disclosed on the Company's website; apart from reimbursement of specified expenses to the Chairman, there is no pecuniary relationship or transaction of the non-executive directors with the listed entity.
- Sustainability is stated as an important focus area, with initiatives aimed at optimising energy and water consumption, managing waste responsibly and reducing the environmental footprint of operations.
- Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) is not applicable to the Company for the period under review, so no BRSR-based ESG targets are disclosed.
- A Vigil Mechanism for directors and employees to report genuine concerns is in place, with the policy published on the investor website; no complaints were received under the policy during the year ended March 31, 2026.
- A Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment at Workplace has been adopted with an Internal Committee constituted to redress complaints, and the Company reports compliance with the POSH Act and with the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 where applicable.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As on March 31, 2026 Sinclairs Hotels had a presence across ten destinations within the country and stated it is in the process of further expansion. During FY2025-26 the Company took on lease a palace-style resort with 90 rooms and fine villas, 'Sinclairs Palace Retreat Udaipur', and commenced operations there on 1st August, 2025 — consistent with the industry's gradual shift towards asset-light and lease-based operating models described in the MD&A. The Directors' Report states that the Company's cash reserves are very strong and that it is presently looking at opportunities to expand by way of both greenfield projects as well as acquiring existing properties on lease, with management continuing to evaluate capital-efficient growth opportunities to support long-term scalability while maintaining a prudent financial structure. Existing hotels and resorts at Siliguri, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Chalsa (Dooars) and Burdwan are described as well positioned to benefit from the West Bengal government's infrastructure roadmap for North Bengal and the hill regions, including a proposed Kolkata–Siliguri expressway. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Trusted, home-grown hospitality brand recognised for quality service, strong food offerings, hygienic operations and transparent business practices
- Presence across ten destinations in India as on March 31, 2026, giving diversified geographic spread
- Debt-free balance sheet — the Directors state the Debt-Equity ratio is not applicable since there are no Borrowings, and that cash reserves are very strong, supporting self-funded expansion
- Long-standing operating record — the 54th Annual Report was presented for FY2025-26
- Cost discipline through dynamic pricing, tight cost controls, efficient manpower deployment, multi-skilling of employees and minimisation of wastage
